Valuation Principles

How FIFO Works in Plain English

Under First-In, First-Out (FIFO), inventory sold is accounted for at the exact unit cost of your oldest available stock batch. When supplier prices rise over time, FIFO ensures your historical costs match your revenues cleanly—preventing profit distortion and over-valuing remaining assets on your balance sheet.

Operational Excellence

Why precision FIFO valuation matters

Three structural advantages of automated chronological batch costing over estimates.

0% Margin Distortion

Accurate COGS & Margins

True Profit Transparency

Eliminate profit distortion during periods of volatile supplier pricing or inflation. Know the exact gross margin realised on every single SKU dispatch rather than relying on blended averages.

Impact:

Protect wholesale agreements against unexpected cost runups.

100% Landed Cost Accuracy

Landed Cost Integration

Complete True Cost

Freight, customs duties, quarantine, port charges, and handling fees are automatically apportioned into each batch's unit cost before FIFO deduction begins.

Impact:

Capture actual container import expenses without manual spreadsheeting.

ATO & AASB102 Compliant

Audit-Ready Asset Valuation

Tax & Financial Compliance

Maintain strict compliance with Australian taxation requirements and financial reporting standards without spreadsheet formula errors or fragmented costing records.

Impact:

Support external audits with detailed batch-level transaction and valuation history.

Certified Ecosystem

FIFO-costed cost of goods sold and stock valuation sync automatically into Xero, so financial reports and the balance sheet inventory value always match what's actually happening in stock — no manual journal entries or reconciliation.
